{{Short description|Plane algebraic curve}}
[[Image:Lemniscate-of-Gerono.svg|thumb|The lemniscate of Gerono]]
In [[algebraic geometry]], the '''lemniscate of Gerono''', or '''lemniscate of Huygens''', or '''figure-eight curve''', is a [[algebraic curve|plane algebraic curve]] of degree four and [[geometric genus|genus]] zero and is a [[lemniscate]] curve shaped like an [[Infinity|<math>\infty</math>]] symbol, or figure eight. It has equation

:<math>x^4-x^2+y^2 = 0.</math>

It was studied by [[Camille-Christophe Gerono]].

==Parameterization==
Because the curve is of genus zero, it can be parametrized by rational functions; one means of doing that is

:<math>x = \frac{t^2-1}{t^2+1},\ y = \frac{2t(t^2-1)}{(t^2+1)^2}.</math>

Another representation is
:<math>x = \cos \varphi,\ y = \sin\varphi\,\cos\varphi = \sin(2\varphi)/2</math>
which reveals that this lemniscate is a special case of a [[Lissajous figure]].

==Dual curve==
The [[dual curve]] (see [[Plücker formula]]), pictured below, has therefore a somewhat different character. Its equation is

:<math>(x^2-y^2)^3 + 8y^4+20x^2y^2-x^4-16y^2=0.</math>

[[Image:Dualger.png|thumb|Dual to the lemniscate of Gerono]]
